image: firmware-stop image (apps/gpu-power-id/fw-start.c with FWS_STOP, bundle row 25, frozen as bundle 20 in sets 21 and 23), set board-bundles-20261025-21
hypothesis: Firmware start, one health check, forced-idle and power-off requests, the 14-step stop and the platform OFF run in one image on port 3-1.
prediction: The health check completes within a few milliseconds by the return slot bit 0 of the kernel CCB command.
conclusion: The start passed (started in 667 µs, and an earlier start reported started 672 µs after the release of the firmware processor). The control read the compatibility record, submitted the health check and kicked once (MTS_SCHEDULE <- 0, read-back, then an interrupt with status 1, cleared), waited 200 ms and failed with error=3 (its deadline), health=0 health_status=0x0, while the shared state read kccb_done=0x1 pow_state=0x3. The firmware executed the command (counted in kccb_cmds_executed, interrupt raised) but did not set bit 0 of the return slot for a health check; the control used the wrong completion test, since upstream sends the health check without a slot and judges the firmware alive by kccb_cmds_executed advancing (pvr_watchdog_kccb_stalled, pvr_power.c:149-187) and the vendor schedules it with no slot (rgxfwutils.h:720-721). No OS connection is needed: the open firmware executed the command with the connection's OS state 0, which upstream never writes. Power state 3 is ROGUE_FWIF_POW_IDLE, idle waiting for host handshake, the state upstream treats as idle (pvr_power_is_idle, pvr_power.c:137-147), from which a forced-idle request is accepted. One kick per command was correct. Fix: pvr_gpu_control_count_executed gives the control the executed count; the command completes when the count has advanced by exactly one and the firmware's read offset has passed the command; pvr_ccb_settle frees the slot and a return word, if written, must be 1.

image: firmware-stop image after the executed-count fix (bundle 20 frozen), set board-bundles-20261025-23
hypothesis: With the executed-count completion test the firmware start, health check, forced idle, power off, 14 register steps, OFF and provider park complete on port 3-1.
prediction: GPU FWS control result=0 phase=4 error=0 health=1 health_status=0x0 within a few milliseconds; GPU FWS compat ... kccb_done=0x1 pow_state=0x3; GPU FWS kccb write=0x1 read=0x1 rtn0=0x0 executed_before=0x0 executed_after=0x1; GPU FWS power ack_idle=0x1 ack_off=0x1 state_idle=0x2 state_off=0x0 (each status_ 0x0 unless the firmware writes the power commands' return words); GPU FWS after kccb_done=0x3 pow_state=0x0 kccb_read=0x3; GPU FWS stop result=0 phase=10 error=0 step=14 count=14; then COMPLETE GPU firmware stop: started, health check executed, forced idle and power off acknowledged, idle, OFF and provider parked, status 0 and a responsive ROM. Failure states: an incompatible record (control error 4), no health completion within 200 ms (error 3) or a firmware event (error 7) keep the firmware running and end the lifetime with a power removal; a power request not acknowledged within 300 ms, an acknowledgement with another power state or a platform OFF fault leave the GPU powered; an idle check not met after the power-off acknowledgement powers the GPU off, ends the supply sample, parks the provider and reports the failure.
conclusion: Every predicted line appeared: the health check completed in 1.9 ms with the executed count going from 0 to 1 and no return word, both power requests were acknowledged with FORCED_IDLE and OFF, and the stop took its 14 steps in 23 ms before the OFF and the park.

hypothesis: Host checks cover the 14-step stop, the control completion test and the firmware-stop image.
narrative: Cost: a power-off adds two commands, two acknowledgement polls and 14 register steps; the health check adds one command. The control and stop budgets (200 ms and 300 ms) and the vendor's 500 ms start bound fit, with the 100 ms report, inside the 1.5 s session deadline and keep the monitor's 500 ms margin. checks/pvr-gpu-stop.c and checks/pvr-gpu-stop-reference.py: the 14-step plan, the interrupt acknowledgement with and without a pending event, 118 retained faults and the upstream comparison with each of the four vendor differences checked (~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/gpu-stop-20261025/); the retained fault count later became 122 with the unacknowledged stop. checks/pvr-gpu-control.c: the board's behaviour (executed, no return word) ends at the deadline when only the return word counts and completes with the executed count; a return word of 1 is recorded; two executions or a bad return word refuse; a count without the read offset past the command waits (81 retained faults, ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/gpu-control-20261025/). apps/gpu-power-id/check.py --fw-stop: nine cases on the linked image with a model of the firmware's side of the kernel CCB, power-sync word and interrupt status that, as on the board, writes no return words and leaves power state IDLE after the health check: the complete run, also with return words; an incompatible record; a health check never consumed; a firmware event; a denied power-off; no power-off acknowledgement; a held idle register after the acknowledgement; a platform OFF fault. With --board-log the same model on the image of set 21 reproduces the board's start, control, compatibility and failure lines. The start of every case is the firmware-start sequence access for access; afterwards every access is an interrupt read or clear, a kick with its read-back, or the next stop step. The GPU service host checks rerun at the stop change; three fixtures that expected the stop's reset now expect none (~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/gpu-fw-stop-regress-20261025/); the edit in checks/pvr-gpu-service.c runs in service cases 1-3; the edits in checks/gpu-draw.c and checks/gpu-draw-repeat.c have never run because both checks fail earlier (gpu-draw.c:118, gpu-draw-repeat.c:41), as before the change, so the service's stop path through those fixtures is unchecked. Image comparison: the firmware-start image's loadable bytes are unchanged (487ee41e, the image that passed on the board); its debug information moves with the source lines.
